notes: Ink (ink_trace_check on the delivered trajectory, checks.ink_trace_check): at the end of Stage 1 subgoal 7 the four digit boxes carry ink 0.10/0.21/0.25/0.24 (strokes of 1, 2, 3, 4; look/ink_final.png); at the end 1-3 keep the same ink and the 4's box is clean (0.000) after the left hand's eraser passes; the gaps between digits stay blank.

Pick-up (subgoal 1) is a handover: no single-hand grasp of the 13 mm marker lying on the table both lifts it under realistic friction and is held by the right YAM (tripods with pads 40 deg above the equator wedge out; an index-middle 'cigarette' clamp lifts it but needs a nearly flat hand 7 cm above the table that the right arm cannot hold: joint 2 at pi / joint 4 at -pi/2, best 6.3 mm off over station shifts). The left hand, which reaches the pen at the Stage 2 layout once the right hand has parked, clamps the marker by its cap between index and middle (grasp_stress_test ok), lifts it to (0.10, 0.42, 0.18) and the right hand takes it there with a thumb-index-middle tripod (pose_from_points in the hand scene with the held pen in place); the right then lifts it. Deviation in method only: Stage 1 has the right hand grasp it from the table; the predicates (held in the right hand at the end, lifted clear) are the same.

Uncap (subgoal 3) is done by the left hand during the handover: it keeps the cap and pulls it 4.5 cm off along the pen axis (the press fit lets go at 96 % of 20.2 mm: equalities_released marker_marker_cap_engaged at frame 445), moves it clear and sets it on the table at the marker's start spot. Those entries carry stage1_indices [3] and plan index 1, so each hand's subgoal labels stay in order (the left hand acts again only in subgoal 2); Stage 1 has the right hand pull the cap. Predicate: apart(cap, marker) > 1 cm at the end of the cap entries.

Eraser (subgoal 2): generate_flat_pinches thumb-index pinch across the short axis (r6's pinch now fails grasp_stress_test at the 6 cm lift); the left hand first returns home (a direct reach passed the wrist Euler singularity) and afterwards holds the eraser aside at (-0.36, 0.27, 0.10) so the right arm can reach the first digit.

Writing (4-7): the pen tipped 72 deg nib-down at yaw -140 (the nib disc's rim keeps the tip site 1.4 mm off the face at 55 deg, past ink_trace_check's 1.2 mm), digits 3 cm x 4.5 cm on the row y 0.28-0.32 at x -0.13/-0.07/-0.01/+0.06 (the human's row: x -0.14..+0.06, y 0.27-0.34), strokes as carries of 2 cm segments with the nib 0.5 mm into the face; the right then lifts the pen clear.

Wiping (8): the eraser turned to yaw 15 deg (the left arm cannot hold it over the 4 at its start yaw 95), centred 3 cm right of the 4 so its pad never reaches the 3, five passes in y with the felt 0.3 mm above the face (a 0.5 mm press pushed the eraser up out of the pinch).
Places: the eraser goes back to its start pose (subgoal 9); the marker is laid flat on the table at the right edge (0.27, 0.44), yaw 160 deg (subgoal 10): its start spot holds the cap.

Stress test of the right tripod: in hand scenes a part held in the air falls during the test (gravity acts; held_in_air only keeps it through the settle), so the tripod was stress-tested with the marker's cap end resting on a rail where the left hand holds it (poses/hs_right_air_post.json, all 15 phases ok, drift 1 mm).
Stations not moved (Stage 2 layout). Stage 2 scene unchanged by Stage 3.

Stage 4 randomization (write_stage4_config ranges): the marker is not randomized -- its pick is a two-hand handover (left carries it by the cap, right takes it in the air), which Stage 4's single-carrier kinematic adaptation does not model (all 3 draws with the marker randomized put a finger into the cap or the two hands into each other); the eraser is randomized dx -0.02..0, dy +-0.015, yaw +-6 deg (toward the board its pick puts the thumb into the board frame). stage4_handoff_check accepted 6 of 6 draws.
